children: Investors are repricing sovereign debt from the U.S. to Europe and Japan as they adjust to a world of structurally higher inflation, larger government deficits and higher neutral interest rates, BondBloxx's JoAnne Bianco says in a note. "The story on government debt might be 'higher for a lot longer' instead of just 'higher for longer'," the senior investment strategist says. The continued sell-off in bonds isn't solely about inflation, she says. "Investors are demanding a higher term premium to hold long-dated government bonds" as concerns are growing about persistent fiscal deficits and elevated government borrowing needs. In addition, investors are being asked to absorb significantly more government debt issuance than they were a decade ago--and are demanding higher yields as compensation, she says.
